system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Shanghai, China. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Shanghai itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Shanghai space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (West Bund/Xuhui, M50/Moganshan Road, The Bund/Rockbund, Jing'an, Former French Concession, Putuo, Pudong) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Shanghai spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Shanghai, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: ShanghART Gallery
galleries.note: Shanghai’s foundational contemporary gallery, with three decades of influence and a landmark roster spanning Zeng Fanzhi, Ding Yi, Xu Zhen and Yang Fudong.

galleries.name: Antenna Space
galleries.note: Internationally respected for an adventurous emerging programme and artists including Cheng Xinyi, Guan Xiao and Cui Jie.

galleries.name: MadeIn Gallery
galleries.note: Xu Zhen’s influential gallery and cultural-production platform, central to Shanghai’s experimental scene.

galleries.name: Almine Rech
galleries.note: A major international gallery whose Shanghai branch brings blue-chip and historically significant artists into sustained dialogue with China.

galleries.name: Perrotin
galleries.note: One of Shanghai’s most visible international galleries, combining globally prominent artists with Chinese and Asian positions.

galleries.name: Long March Space
galleries.note: A defining force in Chinese contemporary art whose permanent Shanghai branch extends its rigorous, institutionally followed programme.

galleries.name: Pearl Lam Galleries
galleries.note: A long-running cross-cultural gallery with strong Asian and international networks, major fairs and a prominent Chinese contemporary roster.

galleries.name: Lehmann Maupin
galleries.note: The influential international gallery’s Shanghai space presents globally established artists and deepens its longstanding engagement with Asia.

galleries.name: AIKE
galleries.note: A leading locally founded gallery known for tightly curated exhibitions and sustained support of Chinese artists with growing institutional profiles.

galleries.name: Capsule Shanghai
galleries.note: An internationally visible, curatorially distinctive gallery particularly strong in emerging, diasporic and psychologically charged practices.

galleries.name: BANK
galleries.note: The gallery established by MABSOCIETY is known for ambitious cross-generational exhibitions and a cosmopolitan, critically engaged programme.

galleries.name: Gallery Vacancy
galleries.note: One of Shanghai’s sharpest younger galleries, with strong fair participation and a programme connecting Chinese and international emerging artists.

galleries.name: Tang Contemporary Art
galleries.note: A major Asian commercial gallery whose Shanghai branch adds a substantial roster of established Chinese and international artists.

galleries.name: Ota Fine Arts
galleries.note: The respected Japanese gallery maintains an important Shanghai platform for leading Asian artists, including historically significant conceptual practices.

galleries.name: YveYANG Gallery
galleries.note: A transnational gallery with a conceptually driven programme and a strong record of introducing younger Chinese artists internationally.

galleries.name: M97 Gallery
galleries.note: China’s most durable specialist gallery for contemporary photography, with significant documentary, conceptual and historical holdings.

galleries.name: Vanguard Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding Shanghai gallery respected for supporting experimental Chinese practices and developing artists over extended periods.

galleries.name: Arario Gallery
galleries.note: An influential Korean-founded gallery with deep experience across Asia and an established Shanghai programme of regional contemporary art.

galleries.name: Danysz Gallery
galleries.note: A Paris-founded gallery with longstanding Shanghai roots, especially influential in street-derived, digital and new-media practices.

galleries.name: Chronus Art Center
galleries.note: China’s leading nonprofit institution devoted to media art, supporting exhibitions, commissions, research and technological experimentation.

galleries.name: ROH
galleries.note: The prominent Indonesian gallery’s Shanghai branch brings a rigorous Southeast Asian and international programme to the city.

galleries.name: Leo Gallery
galleries.note: A durable Shanghai gallery with strong connections across mainland China and Hong Kong and a broad cross-generational programme.

galleries.name: Art Labor Gallery
galleries.note: A long-established independent gallery known for culturally diverse programming and sustained support for Shanghai-based artists.

galleries.name: Matthew Liu Fine Arts
galleries.note: A refined programme spanning contemporary painting, abstraction and works on paper, with active participation in leading Asian fairs.

galleries.name: Don Gallery
galleries.note: A respected local gallery that has steadily developed emerging and mid-career Chinese artists through focused solo exhibitions.

galleries.name: Longlati Foundation
galleries.note: A collector-founded nonprofit presenting ambitious exhibitions and commissions by internationally prominent and emerging artists.

galleries.name: Gallery All
galleries.note: A Shanghai- and Los Angeles-connected gallery influential at the boundary between contemporary art, sculpture and collectible design.

galleries.name: Fosun Foundation
galleries.note: A prominent Bund foundation staging high-profile contemporary exhibitions and commissions in the Heatherwick-designed Bund Finance Center arts building.

galleries.name: Prada Rong Zhai
galleries.note: Prada’s restored historic residence hosts carefully produced exhibitions by major international and Chinese contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Anomaly
galleries.note: A younger gallery with a research-minded programme focused on experimental and emerging practices from China and abroad.

galleries.name: NANZUKA ART INSTITUTE
galleries.note: NANZUKA’s permanent Shanghai platform brings influential Japanese countercultural, pop and interdisciplinary artists into the local scene.

galleries.name: Bluerider ART Shanghai
galleries.note: The Taipei-founded gallery’s Shanghai location presents established international artists and technically ambitious contemporary work.

galleries.name: A+ Contemporary
galleries.note: A critically minded gallery supporting younger Chinese and Asian artists through research-led exhibitions and regional art-fair exposure.

galleries.name: AroundSpace Gallery
galleries.note: A Shanghai gallery with a steady programme of emerging and mid-career Chinese artists, especially painting and conceptually informed installation.

galleries.name: Mao Space
galleries.note: An established M50 gallery presenting contemporary Chinese painting, sculpture and installation with regular fair participation.

galleries.name: Qiao Space
galleries.note: Collector Qiao Zhibing’s exhibition space has mounted focused presentations by important Chinese and international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: CC Foundation
galleries.note: A private nonprofit foundation supporting exhibitions, commissions, residencies and research around Chinese and international contemporary art.

galleries.name: MINE PROJECT
galleries.note: An emerging-oriented gallery recognized for giving younger artists substantial early exhibitions and access to international fairs.

galleries.name: Gallery Func
galleries.note: A young Shanghai gallery noted for internet-aware, digitally inflected and new-generation practices.

galleries.name: Rén Space
galleries.note: A curatorially focused space presenting emerging artists through compact exhibitions, collaborations and public programmes.

galleries.name: J Gallery
galleries.note: A locally rooted gallery with a growing programme of younger Chinese artists and a visible presence at mainland fairs.

galleries.name: TONG Gallery+Projects
galleries.note: An M50 gallery and project platform supporting experimental exhibitions and artists at early and mid-career stages.

galleries.name: Yibo Gallery
galleries.note: A Shanghai gallery with an expanding roster of contemporary Chinese artists and increasingly consistent fair participation.

galleries.name: LINSEED
galleries.note: A young gallery developed from an independent project platform, emphasizing research, experimentation and emerging practices.

galleries.name: Grain Projects
galleries.note: An independent photography platform supporting exhibitions, publishing, research and underrepresented approaches to the photographic image.

galleries.name: A2Z Art Gallery
galleries.note: A Paris–Shanghai gallery presenting Chinese, French and other international artists across painting, sculpture and mixed media.

galleries.name: BROWNIE Project
galleries.note: A contemporary-photography gallery known for introducing younger Asian photographers and image-based artists.

galleries.name: Shanghai Gallery of Art
galleries.note: The gallery at Three on the Bund has played a longstanding role in presenting Chinese and international contemporary art in central Shanghai.

galleries.name: Art+ Shanghai Gallery
galleries.note: A long-running gallery promoting contemporary Chinese artists to both local collectors and international audiences.

galleries.name: FQ Projects
galleries.note: One of Shanghai’s enduring smaller galleries, with a record of supporting emerging artists and works on paper.

galleries.name: WS Gallery
galleries.note: A locally active contemporary gallery presenting younger Chinese artists and participating in Shanghai’s principal art-market events.

galleries.name: DUMONTEIL
galleries.note: The international gallery’s Shanghai operation is notable for modern and contemporary sculpture, particularly animalier and materially focused work.

galleries.name: Ora-Ora Shanghai
galleries.note: The Hong Kong-founded gallery’s Shanghai platform broadens access to its programme of Asian contemporary and cross-disciplinary artists.

galleries.name: WOAW Gallery Shanghai
galleries.note: A younger international gallery bringing highly market-visible figurative painting and emerging global artists to Shanghai.

galleries.name: Noeli Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding M50 gallery connecting Chinese and European artists through accessible but consistently contemporary programming.

galleries.name: Two Cities Gallery
galleries.note: An important specialist in contemporary glass, ceramics, lacquer and other craft-based practices, active in M50 since its early years.

galleries.name: island6 Arts Center
galleries.note: The home of the Liu Dao collective is a durable artist-run venue known for interactive, LED and multimedia work.

galleries.name: Studio Rouge
galleries.note: A veteran M50 gallery with a broad programme of Chinese and international painting, sculpture and mixed-media work.

galleries.name: Gallery 55
galleries.note: A long-established M50 venue showing contemporary Chinese artists and contributing to the district’s public gallery ecology.

galleries.name: OFOTO Gallery
galleries.note: A specialist photography gallery with longstanding attention to Chinese documentary and contemporary image-making.

galleries.name: ArtCN Gallery
galleries.note: An independent Shanghai gallery presenting locally based Chinese and international artists across painting, photography and mixed media.

galleries.name: AM Art Space
galleries.note: A small independent space valued for experimental exhibitions, artist projects and sustained engagement with Shanghai’s grassroots scene.

galleries.name: Goethe Open Space Shanghai
galleries.note: A nonprofit cultural platform supporting contemporary exhibitions, commissions and exchange between artists in China and Germany.

galleries.name: Reflexion Gallery
galleries.note: An independent M50 gallery focused principally on contemporary photography and lens-based work by Chinese and international artists.
